verdict.rationale: Obsidian documents a first-party headless Sync client that keeps a vault in sync without the desktop app and is explicitly aimed at agents and automated workflows. Its docs also say notes are plain Markdown files that other tools can edit, so an agent can read and write notes headlessly through the file layer. However, the evidence shows no documented read/write note API, REST endpoint, or MCP server. Obsidian URI triggers in-app actions, and the plugin Vault API is a developer building block that runs inside the app. missing for 10: a documented local or vendor read/write API or official MCP server for notes, agent-facing query/write semantics beyond raw files, and independent hands-on corroboration of agent workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent or assistant can read AND write my notes headlessly — through a documented local API, vendor API, or MCP server — without me touching the GUI

citations.quote: Obsidian Sync offers a headless client to sync vaults without using the desktop app. Useful for CI pipelines, agents, and automated workflows.
Because notes are plain text files, you can use other text editors and file managers to edit and manage notes.
